column1: # Lunar corpus fixtures — real-world Lua projects swept by LuaCorpusSweepTest.
# Each row is a pinned upstream checkout fetched by fetch-corpus.sh into test/corpus/<name>.
# Pin to release tags (resolved to their commit SHA), never to a moving branch: the sweep is a
# ratchet against a recorded baseline, so the tree must be byte-identical across runs.
# NB: test/luacheck is a DIFFERENT tree — a clone of the internal glimmer/luacheck fork with
# commits that do not exist upstream. It belongs to LuaRecursiveReferenceTest; do not conflate
# the two.
# The optional 5th column deletes non-Lua ballast after checkout so the builder rsync stays cheap
# (luarocks/win32 alone is 11 MB of vendored Windows binaries).
# The optional 6th column pins the Lua language level the sweep runs under. It matters beyond the
# LuaLanguageLevel inspection: the level selects which stdlib globals are known, so an unpinned
# level would make every inspection count a function of LuaProjectSettings' LUA54 default.
# The optional 7th column names the subdirectory module names resolve against, put on package.path
# for the sweep. Omit it when requires are relative to the checkout root, as all three below are.
# It exists for projects that name modules relative to a subtree — KOReader's require("ui/uimanager")
# means frontend/ui/uimanager.lua — where omitting it makes every such require read unresolved.
# name<TAB>url<TAB>commit<TAB>roots<TAB>prune<TAB>luaLevel<TAB>moduleRoot  (roots/prune comma-separated)
luacheck
luarocks
zerobrane
